q: Cut a two-camera concert and keep a full-size master.
a: 1. Select both cameras' clips and run Create Multi-Camera Source Sequence… (`clip.createMulticam`), lined up by audio if there was no shared timecode. 2. Put it on the timeline, switch the Program monitor to the multicam view and cut between angles while playing. 3. Export with the 6.2K Master HEVC preset (6240×4160, Main 10, about 200 Mbps) to keep.

q: Transcribe an interview, cut it by text and add captions.
a: 1. Sequence ▸ Transcript ▸ Transcribe… (`transcript.generate`). 2. Select runs of words and Extract (`transcript.extract`, closes the gap) or Lift (`transcript.lift`, leaves it). 3. Create Captions from Transcript… (`transcript.createCaptions`): by default at most 42 characters per line on two lines; edit them in the Captions tab and style with `captions.setStyle`.

q: Make a draft with a placeholder voice-over and send it for review today.
a: 1. Write the script in the Text to Speech panel, pick a voice and Create (`tts.create`): it imports `Narration <n>.wav` at the playhead on a free audio track. 2. Quick Export (`export.quick`) makes a file next to the project with the last preset used, skipping the Export page. Edit the narration later with `tts.edit`; it keeps its place.

q: My upload site has a size limit; how do I export to fit it?
a: 1. Aim at a size, not a quality: in Bitrate Encoding choose VBR, 1 pass and set the target bitrate. CRF gives an even look but you only learn the size afterwards. 2. Export now from the Export page, or Send to Queue and Start Queue (`export.queue.start`).

q: Strip the ums from an interview and give YouTube a subtitle file.
a: 1. Transcribe, then Remove Filler Words and Remove Pauses (`transcript.removeFillers`, `transcript.removePauses`). 2. Create Captions from Transcript… (`transcript.createCaptions`), check them in the Captions tab, then File ▸ Export ▸ Captions… (`captions.export`) as a sidecar file.

q: Export the YouTube version and the vertical version in one go.
a: 1. Open Export, pick YouTube 4K HEVC for the main sequence and Send to Queue; then the vertical sequence with Vertical 2160×3840 HEVC, Send to Queue. 2. Start Queue (`export.queue.start`): they encode one after another in the background.

q: Send the client a rough draft now and the proper file later.
a: 1. Draft: Quick Export (`export.quick`), the last preset used, saved next to the project. 2. Final: open Export (`file.exportMedia`) and pick the preset for where it's going (e.g. YouTube 4K HEVC), change only what you need, and Export.
